summary: I recommend reject. The evidence holds up for all seven criteria, but one major issue blocks acceptance. Each of the seven acceptance criteria now has committed raw records in the COMMAND/output/RESULT format, and the review-1 blocker and its three majors are fixed. The figures I recounted from the raw files match the README. The controller code has no defect that could make a failed command or gate report a pass. The major issue is SHA256SUMS. README lines 26-28 say the standard verifier (`sha256sum -c`) reports 7 of the 90 entries as FAILED, and that a Node check matched all 90. That Node check has no committed output or exit status. AGENTS.md:43 forbids this, and it is the same kind of defect that caused the review-1 reject. The explanation given (CRLF bytes) does not hold for binary-mode `*` entries, so either the explanation or 7 digests are wrong. Secondary gaps: the clean-checkout check and the protected-path listing were taken before two later amends to the head commit (05d2d42), and some README provenance claims are overstated. All are cheap to fix.

findings.title: SHA256SUMS fails the standard verifier for 7 entries, and the 'all 90 match' check has no recorded output
findings.reasoning: The README says Git for Windows `sha256sum -c` reports the 7 files containing CR bytes as FAILED. I confirmed exactly 7 such files: both install-zig logs, raw/c-assert-negative-control.log, raw/compiler-archive.log, raw/host-versions.log, raw/powershell-diagnosis.log and superseded/hand-captured/c-assert-negative-control.log. The counter-claim that 'a Node check that reads each file as bytes matched all 90 entries' has no log, command or exit status. That violates AGENTS.md:43 and docs/AGENT_OPERATIONS.md:53. The explanation offered is implausible [INFERENCE]: every entry uses the binary `*` flag, and Git for Windows mounts are binary, so CRLF should not change sha256sum's digest. Either the explanation is wrong or the 7 digests were computed on normalized text and do not match the raw bytes. These 7 files include primary evidence for criteria 1 and 2. Every SHA256SUMS digest that also appears as a gate receipt output (all 9 final gate logs) matches its receipt.
findings.reproduction: cd engineering/evidence/FP-0001 && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS. Then compare `certutil -hashfile install-zig-attempt1.log SHA256` and `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').createHash('sha256').update(require('fs').readFileSync('install-zig-attempt1.log')).digest('hex'))"` against 91bb06db…. Fix: commit both checks as `record` logs. Then either regenerate SHA256SUMS from raw bytes or correct the explanation.

findings.title: Commit 89109be is not the full archive, and the worktree manifest check needed an unrecorded copy
findings.reasoning: [INFERENCE] .gitignore excludes out/. The head index (.git/index) has no out/evidence paths. The name-status listing against 89109be in raw/protected-paths.log has no 'D out/evidence/…' lines. So 89109be does not contain the 6 out/evidence entries listed at lines 59-64 of BOOTSTRAP_MANIFEST.sha256. Yet raw/bootstrap-baseline.log reports those 6 as OK in the base worktree, and evidence-check read them there, so someone copied them in without recording it. The digests still prove the bytes match the manifest. The README claims 'the verbatim archive' (line 52) and 'without changes' (line 68) overstate what is in Git history.
findings.reproduction: git ls-tree -r --name-only 89109be -- out | wc -l (expect 0), then git ls-tree -r --name-only 89109be | wc -l.

findings.title: Command records omit the working directory and timestamps
findings.reasoning: COMMAND (line 301) and RESULT (lines 315-318) record the executable, arguments, status and duration, but not the cwd or a start time. `record --cwd` (fairpane.mjs:88) changes how relative arguments resolve. So raw/bootstrap-baseline.log does not show that the `sha256sum -c BOOTSTRAP_MANIFEST.sha256` records ran in out/wt-89109be. The worktree can only be inferred from modified files reporting OK. raw/global-cache-isolation.log cannot show that its scans followed the final gate run.
findings.reproduction: Read raw/bootstrap-baseline.log:2-3 and the record at line 25. No cwd appears.

findings.title: Failure paths around output capture can leak descriptors or crash without a RESULT
findings.reasoning: (a) If fs.openSync(capture,'wx') throws at line 305, runProcess throws synchronously after the log fd (line 300) is opened. That fd leaks, and the log keeps a COMMAND line with no RESULT. runGate's catch still writes a failed receipt, but the commands array lacks the record. (b) Capture-copy failure is handled correctly in the normal case: the record gets an error, the gate fails, and the capture file is removed (lines 312-314). But if the failure comes from writing the log fd itself (for example, a full disk), the writeSync on line 318 also throws inside the 'close' handler. That crashes the controller with no RESULT, no receipt and an open fd. (c) `processError ??=` silently drops the capture error when a spawn error already exists. None of these can produce a false pass.
findings.reproduction: Point os.tmpdir() at an unwritable TMP and call runProcess, or make copyFileToDescriptor's writeSync fail (for example, a read-only log). Observe the leaked fd and the missing RESULT line.

findings.title: The new tests miss several plausible regressions
findings.reasoning: (1) Line 302 'ignores the working directory' passes the temporary directory as resolveExecutable's root argument, not as process.cwd(). A regression that searched process.cwd() would still pass. (2) Line 312 passes the absolute process.execPath, so a regression that logged the unresolved name instead of the resolved path for bare names would pass. Only the failing bare-name path is covered. (3) Line 287 checks that ran.txt is absent but not that nothing was written. A regression that created the log under `tools/` before validating would pass. (4) No test covers capture-copy failure, removal of the temporary capture file, stderr capture, run/record CLI parsing, or runGate's ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR injection (the actual repair). The tests do catch an ignored evidenceDir, a missing environment_overrides, PATH order, failure exit preservation and unapproved log roots.
findings.reproduction: Mutate resolveExecutable to search process.cwd() first, or change recordCommand to pass `executable` instead of `resolved`. The suite still reports 60/60.

findings.title: Probe attribution and contracts are prose
findings.reasoning: The agent type, status and duration columns, and the statement that each probe could call only yield, come from task-tool headers that were not preserved. The fairpane-spec run2 probe and the fairpane-spec run1 probe report no agent name. The tool lists themselves agree with the declared frontmatter.
findings.reproduction: Search probes/*.json for agent type. It is absent or null in several files.

findings.title: The local cache deletion before the final run is prose only
findings.reasoning: No record shows the deletion. The zig-test duration (4407 ms against 64 ms cached) and raw/zig-test-summary.log (fresh --cache-dir, 'run test 7 pass') support the outcome indirectly. zig-build took 112 ms, which suggests the library step may have been a cache hit.
findings.reproduction: Search raw/ for a delete or remove record. There is none.

findings.title: installed_check_evidence cites README prose
findings.reasoning: It points to README.md rather than raw/omp.log or raw/host-versions.log. This is an allowed path, and the policy digest change it causes is explained.

findings.title: Temporary capture file handling
findings.reasoning: The capture is created in the shared os.tmpdir() with the default mode, so on POSIX other users can read it under the usual umask. The catch at line 314 silently swallows a failed removal, which leaves child output in %TEMP%. Output only reaches the log after the child exits, so an external kill of the controller loses it. The watchdog path still copies output.

findings.title: resolveExecutable edge cases
findings.reasoning: Quoted PATH entries are not unquoted. Relative PATH entries resolve against process.cwd(). On Windows a name such as 'python3.12' is treated as having an extension. `record --env PATH=…` resolves through the parent's PATH. The record stays truthful in every case, because the absolute path it logs is the one spawned.

findings.title: Properties the brief asked me to verify all hold
findings.reasoning: evidencePath confines the log path before any command runs (line 376). safePath rejects traversal, absolute paths, ':' and symlinks or junctions. allowed_evidence_roots are matched by prefix plus '/'. spawn uses shell:false, and resolution tries only .com and .exe, so there is no implicit .cmd shell. commands.push runs before the pass invariant, so failure records are kept. The watchdog (taskkill /T /F, then SIGKILL, or a process-group kill on POSIX) is intact, and output from a timed-out child is still copied. On a copy failure the record gets an error, so a pass is impossible. run --evidence-dir parsing rejects a missing or empty value and extra arguments. record parsing consumes only options before the log path, and its exit status is nonzero for any failed record.
